content: The drug osphenytoin reduces the levels or effects of elvitegravir by altering its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to avoid co-administration or consider alternative medications. Co-administration with CYP3A inducers can lead to decreased plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and any concurrently administered protease inhibitors, potentially resulting in therapeutic failure and resistance. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by affecting its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Combining futibatinib with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may heighten the risk and severity of futibatinib-related toxicities. Elvitegravir increases the levels or effects of infigratinib (DSC) by altering its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely for gilteritinib-related adverse effects, and adjust the dosage in cases of severe toxicity. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glasdegib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of idelalisib via CYP3A4 metabolism, and idelalisib also increases the levels or effects of cobicistat. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat through CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of infigratinib (DSC) via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effects. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lapatinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, administer 500 mg of lapatinib daily and adjust the dose after discontinuing cobicistat. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lefamulin via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of leniolisib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. Tenofovir AF decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporters. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, do not exceed 80 mg of levomilnacipran daily. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lomitapide via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg daily. After discontinuing the CYP3A inhibitor, resume the previous lorlatinib dose. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Elvitegravir and lovotibeglogene autotemcel interactions require discontinuation of antiretrovirals (ARTs) at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin via CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the CYP3A inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous lurbinectedin dose. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of midazolam intranasal via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs, as this may prolong sedation. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor for increased adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg daily and monitor closely for adverse effects. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternatives exist, monitor closely for adverse effects. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for adverse reactions.
